content: The dose of deflazacort, a substrate of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and CYP3A4, should be reduced to one-third of the recommended dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 and/or P-gp inhibitors. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Both degarelix and itraconazole can prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. Itraconazole and desipramine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Itraconazole and deutetrabenazine both increase the QTc interval. While deutetrabenazine at its maximum recommended dose does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent, certain conditions (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation) may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. Caution and monitoring are advised. Itraconazole increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexamethasone decreases itraconazole levels via the same pathway. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Itraconazole increases diazepam buccal and intranasal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Didanosine decreases itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution should be administered two hours before or several hours after itraconazole. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases digoxin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Digoxin levels should be measured before initiating concomitant drugs. Monitor therapy and consider reducing the digoxin dose by approximately 30-50% or adjusting the dosing frequency. Diltiazem increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and itraconazole increases diltiazem levels. Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) have negative inotropic effects that may be additive with itraconazole. Monitor for adverse reactions, and dose reduction of concomitant drugs may be necessary. Both dolasetron and itraconazole increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. Both donepezil and itraconazole increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole and doxepin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases doxorubicin liposomal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases dronabinol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases dutasteride levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases duvelisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib AUC, potentially increasing the risk of toxicities. Reduce the duvelisib dose to 15 mg BID when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Elagolix decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered, and consider increasing their dose if needed. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, use caution when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor therapy closely. Itraconazole increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. When co-administered with elvitegravir, the itraconazole dose should not exceed 200 mg/day. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which is metabolized by CYP3A4. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, raising the risk of toxicities. Monitor closely for signs of toxicity. Erythromycin base increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both itraconazole and escitalopram prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and toxicities. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors like itraconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases etoposide levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dosage to half of the recommended dose if co-administered. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases haloperidol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both itraconazole and haloperidol prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole decreases ifosfamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, decreasing its efficacy. Use caution and monitor therapy. Itraconazole increases iloperidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both itraconazole and iloperidone prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy.
